newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Detained French aidworkers await release in Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Detained French aidworkers await release in Kabul.

text.p: Two French aid workers held in Kabul by the purist Islamic Taleban militia said on Thursday they were in good health and appreciated the messages of support they had received.
"Our health is okay, and we started receiving visits yesterday," said Jose Daniel Llorente, interviewed by Reuters in the cell he shares with Frederic Michel.
A senior Taleban official was present throughout the brief interview, conducted in English.
The two Frenchmen, who work for the private Paris-based charity Action Contre la Faim (Action Against Hunger), were detained along with five Afghan staffers last week.
Taleban officials say they are under investigation for "immoral deeds" in connection with a lunch given by ACF's women expatriate staff for Afghan women working for the group.
Armed Taleban fighters raided the ACF compound during the occasion. They later went to a U.N. compound and detained the Frenchmen, neither of whom had been present at the lunch.
Looking clean and relaxed, Michel said they had not been maltreated. "We have had good treatment and for the moment we don't need anything. We are just waiting, but that is OK," he said.
The two men said they had been visited by the International Committee of the Red Cross, a French diplomat and several fellow aid workers, who brought food, books, cigarettes and toiletries.
The Frenchmen are occupying a room four metres (yards) by five metres (yards) in the compound of the Ministry of Accountability -- formerly the Ministry of National Security.

Their cell had bars on the window and a wooden door, which was unlocked during the interview. It was furnished with cushions on the floor, in the traditional Afghan fashion, and had a wood-burning stove to keep out the spring chill.
The aid workers have been allowed to walk in the small garden outside their jail for a few hours each day.
The United Nations and the French government have urged the Taleban to release the Frenchmen immediately.
